$comment: Baseline styling rules sent with every outfit request. Plain language; edit freely. They apply to every wardrobe.

rules.rule: Build around one or two main colors. Neutrals (black, white, grey, navy, beige, camel, denim) go with anything; pair at most one strong color with neutrals unless the person's palette leans bright.
Tonal outfits (shades of one color) and monochrome looks are deliberate and count as harmonious.
One bold pattern per outfit. Two patterns only if they differ in scale and share a color; solids anchor patterns.
Keep pieces within one formality step of each other; shoes and outerwear set the tone, so match them to the occasion first.
Balance volume: a loose or oversized piece pairs with a fitted one. Fitted top with wide bottoms, or relaxed top with slim bottoms.
A cropped or short top works with high-waisted bottoms; a long top works over slim bottoms.
Heavy fabrics (wool, corduroy, velvet, fleece) for cool and cold days; light ones (linen, cotton, silk) for warm days. Don't mix summer-only fabrics with winter-only ones.
Rain: skip suede and delicate fabrics, prefer closed shoes. Cold: closed shoes and layers. Hot: breathable, light colors.
Mixing textures (knit with denim, leather with cotton) adds interest in an otherwise simple outfit.
Accessories are optional; add one or two at most, matching the outfit's metals and formality.
